text: This staff report is about a matter that Community Council has delegated authority from City Council to make a final decision. Transportation Services has reviewed the need for traffic calming (speed humps) on Harlton Crescent, between Silverthorn Avenue and Haverson Boulevard. The assessment indicates the warrant criteria as set out in the City of Toronto's Traffic Calming Policy has not been satisfied. Therefore, staff do not recommend the installation of speed humps on Harlton Crescent.

The Etobicoke York Community Council: 1. Waived the petition and polling requirement under the City’s Traffic Calming Policy and authorize the installation of one traffic calming device (speed hump) at 30 Harlton Crescent. 2. Directed the City Solicitor to prepare a by-law to alter the roadway to install one speed hump at 30 Harlton Crescent, generally as shown on Attachment 2 to the report (August 23, 2021) from the Acting Director, Traffic Management, Transportation Services (Drawing 421G-3921).
